candidate: G9 typed numeric canonicalization candidate v0.1
semantic_property: Typed numeric semantic identity must be invariant across host serialization/lowering surfaces for the same represented ClayCode value; host presentation bytes must not define semantic identity.

corpus.float64_generation: raw 64-bit patterns including signed zero, finite normals/subnormals, infinities and NaNs

observed.python_nan_inf_json: nonstandard NaN/Infinity tokens when allow_nan default is used

expected_vs_observed: Expected host-native formatting divergence and exact typed-token stability. Observed 204 native float presentation mismatches, multiple integer precision counterexamples, and zero candidate-token mismatches on the bounded corpus.
limitations: No production G9 parser/canonicalizer/compiler was exercised.
No Ubuntu developer-system execution receipt was produced.
The experiment establishes representation-level differences, not cross-backend floating arithmetic equivalence.
The candidate NaN normalization rule is not promoted for domains where NaN payload/sign may be intentionally observable.
